messages:
Jamal H.: FYI hitting a surge of 401s starting ~08:12 UTC after the auth key canary rollout. Support already has 3 tickets saying 'authentication failed' for token-auth endpoints. Sample curl from a customer: 
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
* HTTP/2 401
* server: envoy
< HTTP/2 401
{"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"kid not found"}
```
Logs from auth-service show repeated `kid mismatch` on validation: 
```
2026-03-15T08:12:21Z auth-validator [WARN] token validation failed: kid=abc123 not in current-keyset
2026-03-15T08:12:21Z redis-cache [INFO] lookup keyset:v2 -> miss
2026-03-15T08:12:21Z auth-rotation [INFO] started rotation job for env=prod, shard=canary
```

Sara L.: escalated to incidents, adding oncall. I just pinged the impacted customers to acknowledge. Opening ticket: INC-2026-03015-AUTH. Putting this channel as the primary thread.

Morgan (oncall): I'm on it. initial read: rotation job triggered across the fleet but the canary group got the new JWKS pushed before the cache invalidation propagated to the validator pods. validator still using cached keyset v1 while rotation published new kid in v2 -> resulting kid lookup fails. digging into cache TTL metrics.

Taylor I.: that sounds like a propagation race — did the rotation job include an explicit barrier to wait for all validators to reload? We pushed the new code to rotation-controller last week; maybe the ordering changed.

Morgan (oncall): looking at rotation-controller logs: 
```
rotation-controller: publish jwks v2 -> ack from config-store
rotation-controller: mark trigger complete -> enqueue cache-invalidate (async)
```
So we're seeing async invalidation. The canary pods used the new tokens immediately while validators didn't see invalidation fast enough.

Jamal H.: customers are hitting retries and some automated clients are repeatedly failing (hitting rate limits as a side-effect). Support requests also say some throttling shows in their metrics. We should mitigate first.

Morgan (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) pause further rotations (rotation-controller -> pause). 2) roll back canary to v1 key immediately. 3) force cache purge on validators. I'll run commands now.

Morgan (oncall): running forced purge: 
```bash
# purge via redis and trigger in-process reload
kubectl exec -n infra deploy/auth-validator -- redis-cli del keyset:current && kubectl rollout restart deploy/auth-validator -n infra
```
Executing rollback of canary keypackage: 
```bash
rotation-controller rollback --target=canary --version=v1 --reason="propagation race causing 401s"
```

ops-bot: rollback job submitted (id=rb-1937654321). Notifying CDNs and edge caches.

Morgan (oncall): after forced purge + rollback we see 200s returning for the previously impacted requests. Monitoring for 10m to confirm stability. Early gauge: 401s dropped from ~120/min to ~3/min in 5 minutes.

Sara L.: I've updated the customers and escalated to enterprise success for any SLA impact. Also flagged billing implications for repeated retries — finance noted potential adjustments if cost impact > $X.

Taylor I.: root cause hypothesis: rotation-controller changed to publish keys then enqueue async cache invalidation. Older behavior did synchronous invalidation+confirmation across validator workers before accepting tokens. We need a follow-up: make invalidation synchronous for canary/first wave or include versioned token acceptance window with old-v1 accepted for X seconds.

Morgan (oncall): agree. Immediate postmortem action items: 
- Add a sequencing/ack barrier to rotation-controller so that publish -> confirm invalidation -> mark complete (low latency ack path).
- Add integration test: rotation publish + simulate cache lag -> verify no 401s for mixed fleet during window.
- Add metrics and alert on kid-mismatch rates > 5% sustained for 2m.
- Add a canary policy to delay token issuance until validators report a successful reload.

Jamal H.: repro steps I used for QA: 
1) start validator pods with stale cache TTL artificially high (redis keyset:ttl=3600)
2) publish jwks v2 to config-store via rotation-controller
3) issue tokens signed with v2 to a canary node
4) send requests to validators -> see kid mismatch.

Commands: 
```bash
# simulate stale cache
redis-cli set keyset:v1 '{...}' EX 3600
# publish new jwks
rotation-controller publish --jwks-file ./jwks-v2.json --env=prod
# issue token (local tooling)
./token-issuer --kid=abc123 --payload '{"sub":"test"}' > token.jwt
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat token.jwt)" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -i
```

ops-bot: incident status -> mitigated. Please prepare a short post-incident and assign owners.

Sara L.: assigning owners in the ticket: 
- Rotation reliability (Taylor I.)
- Validator cache robustness (Morgan)
- Customer comms & billing followup (Sara)
- QA harness + regression tests (Jamal)

Taylor I.: I'll open a PR today to change the controller to wait for invalidation acks; will include a feature flag. Also will add a fallback acceptance window: validators accept previous keyset for 60s after publish.

Morgan (oncall): leaving notes here: immediate rollback worked, but we saw 3 lingering 401s from long-lived client sessions that embedded tokens from the now-rolled-back canary. We'll coordinate a follow-up sweep to rotate those tokens or notify customers.

Jamal H.: thanks team. I'll draft the postmortem and include the reproducible steps and the tests. tagging for follow-up: @Taylor I., @Morgan (oncall), @Sara L. :thumbsup:
